chunks: Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no forgetfulness (sahw) upon the Imam, and no forgetfulness upon those behind the Imam, and no forgetfulness upon forgetfulness, and no re-performance (i'adah) upon re-performance."

key_terms.سَهْوٌ: Forgetfulness or minor error in prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on forgetfulness (sahw) for the Imam and the followers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential principle that the Imam’s forgetfulness does not invalidate the prayer for the followers, nor does the Imam’s own prayer suffer from 'forgetfulness of forgetfulness' (sahw al-sahw). It establishes a clean legal chain where re-performance (i'adah) is a final act, preventing an infinite regress of errors, thereby ensuring stability in congregational worship.
